design_analysis: Identify statutory authority and the administrative-simplification context; retain as interpretive context rather than a separate operating safeguard.
Determine whether the actual legal entity and function are covered; assess business-associate duties under the applicable subparts.
Resolve covered entity, business associate, subcontractor, workforce and PHI definitions against actual functions; a vendor label alone does not establish status.
Monitor changes to standards and specifications; do not treat modification mechanics as a deployed control.
Determine applicable transition dates for new or modified requirements from the actual rule and entity facts.
Retain statutory preemption authority for legal analysis of competing obligations.
Apply the defined tests for contrary and more-stringent law before resolving state/federal conflicts.
Assess preemption exceptions and more-protective state law using actual data, jurisdictions and service roles; do not assume HIPAA is the only applicable privacy law.
If an exception determination is sought, legal owns the submission, factual basis and correspondence.
Track the duration and changing factual basis of any exception determination before relying on it.
Identify scope of compliance and investigation provisions for the regulated entity.
Retain the reserved section in the inventory; propose no substantive control obligation.
Support cooperation and compliance assistance without treating assistance as an assurance opinion.
Route regulatory complaints to legal; preserve complaint facts, dates and protected reporting channels.
On a compliance review, preserve relevant records and coordinate truthful responses through legal.
Maintain required records and cooperation/access capability for HHS investigations; bind response scope and custodians to the actual request.
Track investigation findings, resolution terms and enforcement communications through legal.
Validate subpoenas and inquiries, preserve responsive evidence and track response obligations.
Prohibit intimidation and retaliation for protected participation; separate investigation access from personnel decisions and preserve complaint handling evidence.
Record applicability of civil-money-penalty provisions; this is enforcement context, not a recurring technical test.
Apply penalty-subpart definitions when analyzing exposure and defenses.
Analyze potential violations and agency relationships from actual facts; vendor outsourcing does not remove all regulated-entity exposure.
Verify current penalty amounts from applicable primary inflation-adjustment sources if exposure modeling becomes necessary; do not hard-code a stale amount.
Preserve timing and occurrence evidence needed to analyze repeated violations.
Preserve harm, history, financial and other relevant facts for penalty-factor analysis.
Evaluate affirmative defenses and correction timing using evidence; remediation does not automatically establish a defense.
Legal evaluates waiver conditions and records any request and disposition.
Legal tracks limitations periods from actual facts and applicable authority.
Route settlement authority and proposed terms through authorized legal/governance approval.
Consider other available legal consequences separately from civil money penalties.
Log receipt of a proposed determination and immediately docket response/hearing deadlines.
Track consequences of failing to request a hearing; preserve proof of timely filing.
Coordinate any penalty collection through legal and finance with authorized settlement/payment records.
Assess regulator public/agency notification consequences and prepare accurate authorized communications.
Retain hearing-procedure scope for a triggered enforcement matter.
Apply hearing-subpart definitions to the case record.
Docket any request for an ALJ hearing and preserve filing/service evidence.
Record party rights, authorized representation and case participation decisions.
Track ALJ orders and comply with lawful procedural directions.
Control case communications to avoid prohibited ex parte contacts.
Prepare authorized representatives and preserve prehearing orders and commitments.
Use authorized settlement review and retain final agreement and implementation duties.
Preserve discoverable material, validate requests and record production scope, holds and objections.
Docket required witness/exhibit exchange and preserve versioned submissions.
Validate attendance subpoenas and coordinate witness compliance through legal.
Track applicable witness fees and authorized payments if a hearing occurs.
Validate filing form, service method and proof for each case submission.
Compute case deadlines using the applicable time rule and independently check the docket.
Route motions and responses through counsel; preserve filed versions and service.
Track procedural compliance and any sanctions; escalate missed orders and deadlines.
Assess preclusion effects of prior determinations using the actual case record.
Prepare and preserve hearing proceedings through authorized representation.
Assess regulator statistical sampling in an enforcement matter; do not reuse it as an assurance sample-size rule.
Prepare witnesses and preserve authorized testimony handling and required attendance.
Maintain evidence provenance and address admissibility under the hearing rules.
Reconcile the official hearing record and preserve authorized copies and corrections.
Docket and submit authorized post-hearing briefs with filing evidence.
Record the ALJ decision, consequences and next deadlines.
Evaluate appeal rights and deadlines; retain authorization and filings.
Track any requested or granted stay and its effect before relying on it.
Counsel assesses procedural error under the applicable standard; do not infer that a control failure is harmless.
Retain statutory basis for the security/privacy requirements.
Apply organizational and workforce definitions to the actual contracting and operating entities.
Confirm applicability using actual covered-entity/associate functions; reference approval alone is not entity classification.
Assess hybrid/affiliated entity arrangements only if facts support them; the reference scope does not create a designation or combined entity.
Read Part 164 together with applicable general provisions and other parts.
For the proposed associate/subcontractor role handling ePHI, design Security Rule safeguards for actual created, received, maintained or transmitted information.
Apply security definitions to systems, media, access and incidents before choosing safeguards.
Document risk-based safeguard selection, continuing review and every addressable determination; addressable does not mean optional and equivalent alternatives need documented analysis.

Implement risk analysis/management, accountable security responsibility, sanctions, activity review, workforce/access management, awareness, incident response, contingency, evaluation and associate arrangements; preserve required/addressable distinctions.
Design facility access, workstation use/security and device/media handling for corporate administration and both sites; obtain provider evidence and document local duties and addressable analysis.
Specify access control, audit, integrity, identity authentication and transmission safeguards; document encryption/decryption and automatic-logoff addressable decisions and emergency access.
Flow required security duties, reporting and subcontractor safeguards through associate agreements; analyze any special organizational arrangements separately.
Maintain written security policies and required documentation, retain it for six years from creation or last effective date as applicable, make it available and update it after relevant changes.
Retain historical initial compliance dates; they do not grant a new implementation grace period for this service.
Determine breach-subpart scope from unsecured PHI and the regulated relationship.
Assess whether an impermissible use/disclosure is a breach, considering exceptions and the documented four-factor compromise assessment; establish unsecured-PHI status before applying notice duties.
Individual notice is a covered-entity duty; support facts and any expressly delegated delivery without replacing the associate's upstream duty.
Media notice depends on the covered entity's affected population and jurisdiction; support analysis and delegated execution only under defined authority.
Support the covered entity's reporting to HHS and accurate affected-person facts; do not automatically assign its notification role to the associate.

Notify the upstream entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, subject to lawful delay; honor shorter contract terms and provide available affected-person/details information with follow-up.
Record authorized law-enforcement delay, its basis and duration; oral requests require documentation and the specified limited delay unless written documentation follows.
Preserve proof supporting notices or a no-notice determination and apply the administrative provisions cross-referenced by the rule.
Identify direct associate requirements and any delegated covered-entity functions; Privacy Rule obligations are not identical for every actor.
Resolve designated-record-set and purpose definitions from actual data/services; definitions influence access support and permitted use.
Restrict associate uses/disclosures to law and agreement; analyze minimum-necessary exceptions, required disclosures, subcontractor assurances and affected judicial-status provisions.

Build an agreement matrix for permitted uses, safeguards, reporting, subcontractors, rights support, regulator access and return/destruction; address known material violations and delegated functions.
Treatment/payment/operations permissions are not blanket authority for an associate; verify the upstream function, agreement and applicable limits before use/disclosure.
Where an authorization is required, validate its scope, required elements, expiry/revocation and proposed use; route decisions through privacy/legal and the upstream agreement.
Printed attestation provisions are affected by the court vacatur described by HHS; do not activate an attestation workflow solely because this section appears in the XML.
Agreement/objection opportunities concern specific covered-entity disclosures; support only an authorized applicable workflow and record its conditions.
Evaluate each permitted disclosure condition and actual legal demand; permission is not always an obligation and does not authorize every associate disclosure.
Validate de-identification method, limited-data-set agreement or minimum-necessary implementation as relevant; removing obvious identifiers alone is not sufficient.
Determine whether notice duties attach to the actual actor or delegated function; segregate vacated paragraphs from remaining notice amendments and confirm operative requirements.
Route restriction/confidential-communication requests to the responsible covered entity and implement accepted restrictions within the contracted workflow.
Identify the designated record set and support timely upstream access with secure identity checks and traceable delivery; contract turnaround must allow the covered entity to meet its duty.
Support accepted amendments with retained history and downstream updates; legal/covered-entity authority resolves denials and disputed records.
Keep information needed for applicable disclosure accounting and its exceptions; reconcile disclosures across subcontractors where required by the agreement.

Analyze covered-entity administrative duties, express associate requirements, delegated functions and breach-rule cross-references; maintain complaint, sanctions, mitigation, nonretaliation and documentation workflows as applicable.
Assess legacy authorizations/arrangements only if actual historical facts invoke transition provisions; do not use them as a new-service exemption.
Retain historical privacy compliance dates; verify later amendments separately.
Retain severability context without inferring which printed provisions remain operative; reconcile the actual judgment and subsequent authoritative status.
